entries.name: Cameron Bishop

expected.charges: Three counts of sabotage under the Federal Sabotage Act (originally).
expected.sentence:
Three concurrent 7-year terms (vacated 1977 by 10th Circuit; final disposition unclear in available open sources).

Verdict as recorded: Yes (1975); conviction vacated on appeal 1977

Charges as recorded: Three counts of sabotage under the Federal Sabotage Act (originally) for bombing four high-voltage power transmission towers in Colorado over an eight-day span in January 1969. Reduced to lesser charges after the Tenth Circuit reversal at 555 F.2d 771 (1977).

updates.convicted: Conviction reversed; indictment ordered dismissed on May 5, 1977
updates.sentence: Three concurrent seven-year terms. On May 5, 1977, the Tenth Circuit reversed and directed dismissal of the indictment. Defense attorney Hal Haddon recalled that Bishop received an appeal bond and did not serve the prison sentence. His March 12, 1975 arrest is documented by the FBI and a contemporary letter from Mary Bishop; the dates and duration of any pretrial detention remain unverified.

entries.rationale: FBI and contemporary family letter independently establish March 12 arrest. Court ordered dismissal, not reduced charges. Attorney describes appeal bond and no service of prison sentence. Clear unsupported sentencing-as-incarceration start; do not equate arrest with a verified detention interval. Preserve biography and all unrelated fields. Both existing case records retained; possible duplicate flagged for separate review.
